items.title: Stripe Failed Payments: The Complete Guide to Recovery in 2026
items.summary: Every subscription business running on Stripe has felt the sting of a failed payment. A customer who loves your product, uses it daily, and never intended to leave—suddenly churned. Not because they wanted to cancel, but because a credit card expired, a bank flagged a transaction, or funds were temporarily short. This is involuntary churn, and it is one of the most overlooked revenue leaks in SaaS and eCommerce. Failed payments account for a massive share of total subscriber losses across industries. According to Stripe's own Billing report, 43% of businesses don't even know how much revenue they've lost due to involuntary churn or payment failure—yet 72% say fighting churn remains a top priority. The disconnect is staggering, and the opportunity for recovery is enormous.

items.title: Personalized Dunning Emails That Work: Best Practices
items.summary: When it comes to reducing involuntary churn, personalized dunning emails can be a game-changer. A dunning email is a communication sent to customers whose payments have failed, reminding them to update their payment information or settle their balance. While this may sound simple, the way you approach dunning emails can make the difference between retaining a customer and losing them for good. In this article, we’ll explore the best practices for creating personalized dunning emails that work and provide examples to inspire your own efforts.

items.title: Involuntary churn 101: what is it and how it relates to Failed Payments
items.summary: Involuntary churn occurs because of factors outside the customer’s control, such as payment failures or banking issues. For subscription-based businesses, customer retention is the backbone of sustainable growth. Yet, even with the best products or services, companies face a silent but significant revenue leak: involuntary churn. This often-overlooked phenomenon, caused primarily by failed payments, can lead to a staggering loss of recurring revenue. But what exactly is involuntary churn, and how can businesses combat it effectively?
